scope: Spec review of the uncommitted issue #50 change that defers the T07 amendment and data policy approval to the correction receipt, rewrites the repeated-requests construction text, adds a repository-cost statement, and adds loader enforcement plus a test.

checks.question: 1. Protocol changes confined to the named fields
checks.detail: Parsed-JSON diff against HEAD shows only the 8 paths in changed_protocol_paths. partition, budget, ceilings, questions, case_matrix, code_commit/code_paths, oracle_policy, legacy_inputs, freeze (incl. supporting_artifacts), correction_approval, p9, claim_limits and every other recipes field are unchanged.

checks.question: 2. Bound files byte-identical and listed hashes match
checks.detail: git diff HEAD is empty for MANIFEST.json, inputs/, oracles/, certificates/, independent-review.json, quality-review.json, authoring-validation.json and all of evaluation/inquiry-p8; no untracked files besides an ignored __pycache__. freeze.manifest_sha256, all 15 supporting_artifacts, generator/independent_audit_tool/certificate_producer sha256 and all 10 additional_helpers match current bytes. New protocol SHA256 is 5a79bd51..., previous 41a4fa01... as stated.

checks.question: 3. Repeated-requests wording true
checks.detail: All 96 cases have expected_result_kind 'results'. Over the 16 repeated-requests cases every expected_counters.values[k] is below effective_declared_limits[k]; max ratio is pairs 352/1000 (T01-repeated-requests-8), next 264/1000 pairs (T05-8), 169183/1000000 source-bytes. The embedded-events limit (8) has no counter value, but expected_embedded_event_count is 0 for all 16 cases, so it is also below its limit.

checks.question: 4. repository_cost accurate
checks.detail: du: capture 61M (62,499,109 B), replay 61M (62,494,088 B); lean.gz is 41,928,158 B (about 42 MB). Per-directory and binary figures are right. But 'adds about 120 MB to Git history' is false: capture and replay share byte-identical binaries (same blob ids for lean.gz, native.gz, consumer.gz) and Git stores each blob once. Unique blob bytes for the failed capture+replay are 62,157,177 B and on-disk object size is 47,540,287 B. The failed attempt also committed a 6.1 MB preflight-<run-id> directory and a reproduction receipt that the cost statement and data_policy directories omit.

checks.question: 5. Self-consistency and loader enforcement of approval_location
checks.detail: After approval the frozen protocol states the items are approved in the receipt rather than claiming 'proposed'. For status requires-correction-receipt the loader requires receipt approved_amendments[id] with non-empty approval_text and interpretation_sha256 == sha256(interpretation UTF-8); it requires data_policy.state == requires-correction-receipt and receipt.data_policy_sha256 == sha256(json_bytes(data_policy)) (sorted keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False, trailing newline). Non-deferred amendments must carry provenance user and approval_text (source-axis-groups does). Runs only on the non-@1 path after candidate snapshot comparison, so the snapshot equality forces the same deferred items. Loader 'binds' approval_text only as non-empty (see low finding).

checks.question: 6. README accuracy
checks.detail: README matches loader field names (approved_amendments, approval_text, interpretation SHA256, data_policy_sha256) and the refusal behavior. It repeats the 120 MB Git-history claim (see finding) and says 'canonical-JSON' without naming the trailing-newline json_bytes form.

checks.question: 7. No weakening of the original suite
checks.detail: evaluation/inquiry-p8 is byte-identical to HEAD; nothing there pins the loader hash. require_receipt_approvals runs only when recipe version is not inquiry-p8-recipes@1. load_suite(evaluation/inquiry-p8/MANIFEST.json) still succeeds and the @1 generator --check passes. The change adds checks to the corrected path and removes none.

checks.question: Commands run
checks.detail: test/inquiry_approval_receipt.py: 3 tests OK; test/inquiry_corrected_candidates.py: 16 tests OK; inquiry_evaluation_cases.py corrected --check: 96 cases checked; independent_finite_audit.py: AUTHORING-CHECK, 80 exact checks, no findings; inquiry_evaluation_cases.py --check (original) OK. No driver or consumer run.

findings.detail: data_policy.repository_cost (frozen at approval) and README say one new capture plus replay 'adds about 120 MB to Git history'. Git deduplicates identical blobs; the failed attempt's capture and replay share their binaries, so their unique content is about 62 MB (47.5 MB on disk as Git objects). The statement also omits the preflight-<run-id> directory (about 6 MB) and reproduction receipt that the failed attempt committed. Suggested fix: say about 120 MB in the working tree and about 50-62 MB of new Git objects (less if binaries match earlier blobs), and name the preflight directory, or state 120 MB explicitly as an upper bound.

The amendment approval_location says the receipt binds approval_text, but the loader only checks that approval_text is non-empty; any text passes. Only the interpretation is bound by hash. Reword to 'carries a non-empty approval_text'.

approval_location and README say 'canonical JSON' for data_policy_sha256. The loader uses json_bytes: sorted keys, ',' and ':' separators, ensure_ascii=False, UTF-8, trailing newline. A researcher hashing without the newline gets a mismatch. Name json_bytes or spell out the encoding.

The bound independent-review.json and quality-review.json (byte-frozen) attest scripts/inquiry_evaluation_manifest.py at b02308a1..., while recipes.additional_helpers now pins ee99de32.... The protocol does not list any supplemental review covering the new loader in supporting_artifacts, so the frozen protocol does not tie the delta to a review. Consider binding the supplemental spec/quality receipts before approval.

require_receipt_approvals assumes well-formed receipt entries. A non-object approved_amendments entry raises AttributeError, not ValueError. Duplicate ids silently keep the last entry. Refusal still happens, but the error is not the loader's usual diagnostic.
